title: Staff Product Designer, Guest & Discovery
description:
Staff Product Designer, Guest & Discovery

Company

Collaborative Boating operates Boatsetter and GetMyBoat, the two largest marketplaces for getting on the water, now converging into one platform. Guests arrive wanting something specific - a fishing trip, a sunset cruise, a birthday on a pontoon - and we connect them to the captains, operators, and owners who can make it happen. Finding and booking a day outside should be as easy and intuitive as booking a flight.

The problem

Search is changing under us. Guests arrive with intent expressed in natural language, increasingly through an AI assistant instead of a search box, and increasingly on a surface we don't own. Answering that with a chatbot is the obvious move and the wrong one: choosing between boats is a parallel, visual, comparison task, and a conversation is sequential. The work is holding both - a visual discovery experience built for comparison, and a compact, structured expression of a listing that holds up when a third-party assistant renders it in a layout we didn't design.

The center of gravity is the search results card. It's the smallest unit of persuasion we have: a handful of facts, ordered, that a guest uses to decide whether to look closer. Which facts earn a place, in what order, and how that adapts from "boat rental Miami" to "something fun for eight people Saturday" - that's the problem. It's an information design problem before it's a visual one.

What you'll own

•
The end-to-end guest discovery experience - search, filtering and refinement, results, map and list, the listing page, and the paths in from organic search and AI assistants. Coherence across both brands and web plus mobile is yours.

•
The information hierarchy of the results card, defended with evidence, across guest intents and every state the data actually produces: missing photos, no reviews yet, a price range instead of a price, partial availability.

•
Interfaces over a system that infers. Make what it inferred legible, make correcting it easy, and reduce verification labor rather than creating it - a guest who has to double-check our answer has been handed our work.

•
Surfaces we don't render. With engineering, shape the structured expression of an experience, an offer, and an operator so it survives being summarized, quoted, or laid out by someone else's assistant.

•
Continuous discovery with your pod - a Product Manager and an engineering tech lead. Choose the cheapest artifact that answers the open question; spend fidelity when a decision is actually being committed.

How we work

Five things worth knowing before you apply. They aren't universal, and here they aren't negotiable.

Problem, then system, then experience

We frame the problem, then settle the shape of the system - entities, states, edge cases - and only then design the experience within it. Your rough exploration runs alongside the system design and improves it; committed fidelity comes later. In practice that means days of useful work before there's a screen worth showing, and arguing about data models with your tech lead while the design is still loose. If you need a settled brief before you can start, this will be frustrating.

Discovery is ongoing, not a handed off spec

You talk to guests and operators directly. You bring opportunities forward rather than receiving them. There's no research team handing you findings and no Product Manager writing you requirements - the pod owns the outcome and you're one third of it. We believe the commercial results follow from understanding these customers better than anyone else does, which is why the understanding isn't delegated to a function.

We ask what moved, not what shipped

You define the signal before release and watch it after. Hitting the number you set is the floor, not the finish - the work worth remembering beat it, and we'd rather you aim at that and miss than aim at the floor and land. Sometimes the answer is that your design didn't work, you say so plain

SpaceXAI is seeking a Turbine Technician to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot gas turbine generator packages at our power generation facility. • Operate, inspect, and maintain gas turbine generator packages (including Solar and 6000-class units) and associated auxiliaries: lube oil, hydraulic, fuel gas, inlet air, enclosure ventilation, cooling, fire/gas detection, and generator systems

• Support scheduled turbine outages: filter changes, inspections, OEM work, system isolation, and return-to-service

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate

• 3+ years of hands-on experience as a technician or operator working on gas turbines, rotating equipment, or industrial mechanical, electrical, and/or control systems

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

title: Senior Creative Strategist

About Sidekick

At Sidekick , we help people recover faster from injuries. Trusted by Olympic champions and everyday athletes, our products have been featured in Men's Health and Running Magazine . With 94% of users finding relief, we aim to be the go-to injury relief brand.
The role
A lot of performance creative work goes into creating demand that wasn't there. That's not the problem here. Our customer already wants what we sell. Their heel hurts every morning when they get out of bed, or their ankle rolls on uneven ground and they've stopped trusting it.
What they don't believe is that this is the thing that finally works. They've already bought the insoles, done the stretches, and gone to physio twice. So you have to teach before you can sell, and you have to earn trust from someone who has been let down already. It's a harder brief than most, and a more interesting one.
You'll write our paid social advertising and own angle development and testing, reporting to our Creative Director. Expect to ship around 15 briefs a week, a mix of net-new concepts and iterations on ads that are already working. Your week is writing, research, and feedback to editors.
You don't need a physiotherapy background, but you do need to pick up a clinical concept quickly enough to explain it clearly and honestly in fifteen seconds of camera time.
What you'll do

•
Find new winning angles. Better creative is what lets us spend more, so we need a steady supply of ads that keep working as budgets grow.

•
Open new audiences. Runners, older adults worried about falling, people on their feet all day. Each group buys for a different reason, and every one we crack opens up new demand.

•
Get more life out of winners. Read the data weekly, iterate what's working, retire what's finished.

•
Write the scripts. Short and long-form video, hooks that stop the scroll, dialogue that sounds like a real person. This is most of your week.

•
Direct the edit. Brief and manage editors and creators so the idea survives production.

•
Extend what wins. Take proven angles into landing pages and email.

Requirements
What we're looking for

• 4+ years writing paid social ads that were judged on sales (not brand awareness, engagement etc.)

• Your ads have been responsible for over $100K+/month in ad spend (across all your ads, for a single brand). We'll ask you to walk us through it.

• Proof you can iterate on a winner. Plenty of people can write one good ad; we want someone who gets eight more out of it.

• You've opened a new audience before, and you can name the angle that got you in

• Excellent writing for spoken word, which is a different skill from writing for the page

• Strong direct response fundamentals: offer, mechanism, objection handling, proof

• Experience briefing editors or creators

• Health, fitness or medical device categories are a plus

What we care about
We want people who are ambitious and hold themselves to a high standard. They don't need to be managed closely, and want to be the best at their craft. The volume is real and the feedback is direct. In exchange you'll see more results in a year than most people see in three. If you're looking for something comfortable, this won't be the right fit for you.
Benefits

• Compensation: Top of the market for this role. We’ll share compensation details on the first call.

• Fast-growing company whose mission is to solve chronic pain and injuries

• You’ll see the direct impact of your work on business results

• You’ll be held to a high bar, which means you’ll get better fast

• Fun, approachable yet ambitious colleagues

• Comprehensive health benefits

• Work from home

• Familiarity with search and infrastructure tooling such as Lucene, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Redis, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, Docker, AWS/GCP, gRPC, or Protobuf

The people who do well here have personally owned search quality in production, think end-to-end about relevance, crawling, indexing, serving, latency, and cost, and thrive in ambiguity by shipping, measuring, and iterating quickly without needing a fully defined playbook.

title: Head of People & Organizational Effectiveness
description:
SEEKING.COM
Head of People & Organizational Effectiveness
Organization Design | Talent Selection | Team Effectiveness | Incentive Design | People Science
Location: Remote, US
Company: Seeking.com, STNDRDS, and Standards.com (combined US operating organization)
Reports to: Co-CEOs
Type: Full-Time, Exempt
Compensation: $175,000 to $225,000 base
The Question You Will Spend Your Time Answering
Why do some groups of talented people accomplish extraordinary things together, while other groups of equally talented people become slow, political, or frustrated? And how do we deliberately build the first kind?
If you have spent a meaningful part of your career thinking about that question, often when nobody was paying you to, keep reading.
About Us
Seeking.com is the world's largest premium dating platform, founded by an MIT alumnus and headquartered in Las Vegas. STNDRDS is our consumer media brand; Standards.com is our independent news publication. Together we are a combined US operating organization built on one premise: we exist to create value for the people we serve, not to extract it from them.
We are 50 to 60 people, split between our Las Vegas office and remote roles across the country, and we intend to stay small by design. We grow through leverage per person, not headcount. That makes how our people are selected, organized, and work together the single biggest determinant of what we can accomplish.
The Opportunity
You own the design and effectiveness of the human operating system of the company: what people and structure we need, how we select them, how we organize, develop, and reward them, and how they work together. You are not here to administer HR programs. You are here to make the organization, and every person in it, more effective.
The core question you carry every day:
Do we have the right people, organized the right way, operating under the right conditions and incentives, to accomplish what we are asking the company to accomplish?
When the answer is no, you diagnose before you prescribe. Is it the person, the manager, the structure, the incentives, the team composition, unclear ownership, decision rights, information flow, missing capability, or something nobody else has noticed? Then you design the smallest intervention that fixes the real cause, and you measure whether it worked.
Three ideas shape how we work. The Value Creator System: people earn gain share based on demonstrated repeatable value. The Certainty Framework: design work to create the conditions for eustress (voluntary striving toward something you care about) and remove structural sources of distress. The 10x Operating Principle: growth comes through leverage per person, not added headcount.
What You Will Own
You own the architecture of each area below. Payroll, benefits administration, and onboarding and offboarding logistics are run by our Director of Business Operations. You design the systems; that team helps run them.
1. Organizational Design and Diagnosis
Shape roles, teams, reporting lines, decision rights, and operating models around our strategy. Find overlaps, gaps, unnecessary layers, and structures built for yesterday. Be the company's organizational doctor: the person the Co-CEOs call when something involving people does not make sense. The org chart is an output of your thinking, not the starting point.
2. Talent Architecture, Recruiting, and Selection
The goal is capability per employee, not headcount. Before a role opens, ask whether AI, redesign, clearer ownership, or developing someone already here would solve the problem better. Own recruiting strategy, critical and leadership hiring, succession, and retention of high performers. Build selection methods that predict who will perform here, not who interviews well, and track quality of hire at six and twelve months to learn what actually predicts success. Our mission is to create a world where software builds and improves itself.

We build the platform for self-improving software development, helping the world's largest enterprise engineering teams turn their organizations into autonomous software factories. Customers including Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile run Factory to ship code, review PRs, run tests, and deploy continuously - getting smarter with every cycle.

In 2026, we raised $200M at a $5B valuation, bringing our total funding to over $400M. We are backed by world-class investors and operators including Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Blackstone, Ali Ghodsi (CEO of Databricks), and Frank Slootman (Former CEO of Snowflake).

Factory is hiring a Solutions Engineering Manager to build the Mid-Market Solutions Engineering team. Our Mid-Market Solutions Engineers own the full customer lifecycle, pre-sales and post-sales: discovery, demos, proofs of concept, security and architecture reviews, pilot delivery, and the ongoing adoption and expansion of Factory once a customer is live. You will help build out the team, define how it runs, and own both the technical win and the production outcome for our fastest-growing mid-market accounts.

You will hire and coach the people who do this work, set the standard for how it is done, and stay close enough to the accounts to do it yourself when it matters. You will work directly with Mid-Market Sales leadership, and closely with Product and Engineering. title: Major Gifts & Development Associate
description:
Since our founding, Parity Homes has raised over $15 million - driven almost entirely by our CEO, who has built relationships with major donors, foundations, and community investors from the ground up. We are looking for someone to professionalize and systematize what we’ve built so we can grow in scale without that growth depending on one person.
We are looking for a Major Gifts & Development Associate who brings ambition, drive, and genuine relationship instincts to this work. Someone who is energized by the pursuit - identifying prospects, opening doors, building authentic relationships, and seeing major commitments through to close. Writing is a key part of this role, but it is a means to an end. The end is securing transformational funding from donors giving at the $2M-$5M level.
You will work closely with our CEO to drive major donor cultivation from research through close. You will think strategically, act proactively, and take ownership of the pipeline. You write because it moves people to invest in communities - not because you love formatting reports.
WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Research and profile major donors, foundations, and conference attendees in advance of CEO engagements - so every meeting is maximized.

• Own the follow-up. Draft outreach emails, thank-you notes, and cultivation communications as the CEO, ensuring the right tone, timing, and next step.

• Move donors through the cultivation pipeline - from initial contact to scheduled meeting to funded commitment.

• Identify and track grant opportunities aligned with Parity’s mission and manage submission calendars end-to-end.

• Write compelling grant proposals, letters of inquiry, donor reports, and major gift case statements.

• Prepare the CEO for speaking engagements and conferences by building briefing materials that surface funding opportunities.

• Maintain and update the donor CRM, ensuring the pipeline is always current and actionable.

• Proactively surface new funding strategies and prospect ideas - you don’t wait to be told where to look.

Requirements

• Experience in business development, nonprofit development, major gifts, or a donor-facing fundraising role - we care more about your track record than your title.

• Demonstrated success writing grant proposals or major donor communications that resulted in funding.

• Familiarity with donor cultivation strategy and the major gifts cycle.

• Comfort operating as an extension of a CEO or senior leader - drafting in their voice, representing their brand, and owning the follow-through.

• Experience working in a startup, early-stage organization, or resource-constrained environment is a genuine plus.

• CRM experience (any platform) is helpful but not required.

Who You Are

• You are scrappy and resourceful. You figure things out. You don’t wait for a system to exist, you build one.

• You are relationship-oriented. You understand that major donors are people, not line items, and you know how to cultivate trust over time.

• You are a strategic thinker. You don’t just execute tasks - you see the board and know which moves matter.

• You are an excellent writer. Your words are clear, compelling, and calibrated to the reader - whether that’s a foundation program officer or a high-net-worth individual.

• You are driven by outcomes. You want to land big asks and you measure your own success by impact, not activity.

• You are mission-aligned. You care about equitable development, community ownership, and the kind of work Parity is doing - and that comes through in how you represent the organization.

• You are comfortable working independently in a remote, startup environment with limited hand-holding and high expectations.

• You are energized by building something - you don’t need a fully developed infrastructure around you to do your best work.

• You are drawn to organizations doing real, ground-level work and you want to be close to the mission, not at a remove from it.

title: Director – AI Governance & Adoption
description:
Our client recognises that successful AI implementation extends beyond technology and requires strong governance, organisational readiness, employee engagement, and responsible adoption across all business functions.
The Role
Reporting to the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer, the Director of AI Governance & Adoption will establish the policies, standards, and governance framework required to ensure Artificial Intelligence is deployed responsibly, securely, and consistently throughout the Group.
The role will oversee AI governance, data privacy, regulatory compliance, ethical AI principles, organisational readiness, AI literacy programmes, and enterprise-wide adoption initiatives.
Working closely with Human Resources, Legal, Information Security, Risk Management, and subsidiary leadership teams, the Director will ensure employees are equipped to utilise AI effectively while maintaining appropriate governance and compliance standards.
The Director will also lead enterprise communication strategies, change management programmes, adoption measurement, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Candidate Profile
Candidates should possess extensive experience in governance, enterprise risk, organisational change, digital transformation, compliance, or technology governance.
Strong stakeholder management capabilities, communication skills, and experience leading enterprise-wide transformation initiatives are essential.
Experience developing governance frameworks for emerging technologies or enterprise digital programmes will be considered highly advantageous.
